خُصُوصٌ an inf. n. of 1, trans. and intrans. ―
-b2- [Used as a simple subst., Particularity; peculiarity; speciality, or specialty; as also the inf. ns. ↓ خَصُوصِيَّةٌ , and ↓ خُصُوصِيَّةٌ .] You say, لَهُ خُصُوصٌ and ↓ خُصُوصِيَّةٌ [To him belongs a particularity, &c.], and بِى [in me is &c.]. (A.) [Hence خُصُوصًا Particularly; specially; as also ↓ خَاصَّةً .] Th was heard to say, ↓ إِذَا ذُكِرَ الصَّالِحُونَ فَبَخَاصَّةٍ أَبُو بَكْرٍ وَإِذَا ذُكِرَ الأَشْرَافُ فَبِخَاصَّةٍ عَلِىٌّ [meaning فَخُصُوصًا, i. e., When the righteous are mentioned, then in particular, or peculiarly, Aboo-Bekr is virtually mentioned; and when the shereefs are mentioned, then in particular, or peculiarly, 'Alee]. (L, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
